title: Introduction to JSX and Babel
summary: Walks through the first React code: the single-div HTML shell, rendering an h1 into the root div, what JSX is, how Babel compiles it to plain JavaScript, import vs require, and why render accepts only one top-level element.

concepts.heading: Starter sandbox and project layout
points: The lesson uses a CodeSandbox starter linked in the resources. Fork it (GitHub login) to keep your own copy; free accounts have a limit on draft projects, so download finished projects as a zip.
Files: public/index.html (the only one with code at first), src/index.js (empty) and src/styles.css (empty).
index.html is a bare skeleton: a head linking the stylesheet, and a body with a single div whose id is root, followed by a script tag loading index.js.

By convention a React app always has one div with id root; everything React builds is injected inside it. After the first setup this HTML file is not edited again (except the title), all work happens in JavaScript.

concepts.heading: Installing and loading React packages
points: In CodeSandbox, dependencies are added by searching for them in the Dependencies panel and clicking, instead of npm install in a terminal. Needed here: react and react-dom.
Installing is not enough; each file that uses a package must load it. Old style: const React = require('react'); const ReactDOM = require('react-dom') (module names lowercase).
Modern style: import React from 'react'; import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'. import/export (ES6 modules) organise dependencies better; a later lesson covers them in depth.

concepts.heading: Rendering with ReactDOM.render (lesson's React version)
points: ReactDOM.render(what, where, callback?) takes three arguments: the element to show, the DOM node to put it in, and an optional callback run when rendering completes (not needed here).

What to show:

Hello world!

written directly as JSX with no quotes.
Where to show it: document.getElementById('root') (plain DOM API returning the root div).
Result: an h1 appears on the page although index.html was never changed.

(Extra) In React 18+ (including the Vite reference repo) ReactDOM.render is replaced by createRoot(container).render(element), imported from 'react-dom/client'. Same idea: choose a container, render an element.

concepts.heading: What JSX is and how Babel fits in
points: JSX is HTML-like syntax written inside a JavaScript file, with no special delimiters such as EJS tags.
A compiler converts JSX to ordinary JavaScript before it reaches the browser. That compiler is Babel, which tooling in the React setup runs for you.
Demo: removing the React import breaks the page with React is not defined, because compiled JSX calls React functions (createElement).

Babel is a JavaScript compiler that turns next-generation JS (ES6 and later, arrow functions, map, etc.) into code every browser understands, JSX included. Its website has a Try it out pane showing input and compiled output side by side.

Compiled output for

Hello world!

is a React.createElement('h1', null, 'Hello world!') call.
Equivalent vanilla DOM code needs several lines: createElement, set innerHTML, getElementById('root'), appendChild. JSX gives the same result in one readable line.
Because Babel handles compatibility, ES6+ features can be used freely in React code, which is why the module teaches many of them.

concepts.heading: Only one root element
points: render accepts a single element. Placing an h1 and a p side by side causes a syntax error.
Fix: wrap siblings in one parent such as a div; anything nested in a div still counts as one element, so any number of children can be rendered.
(Extra) Modern React also allows a fragment (<>...</>) as the wrapper to avoid adding an extra div to the DOM; the reference repo App.jsx uses it.

task.name: Render your first JSX
task.starting_point: Starter sandbox with the root div in index.html and empty index.js
task.goal: Display an h1 and a paragraph using React
steps: Change the page title in index.html to JSX.
In index.js, add react and react-dom as dependencies and import both.
Call ReactDOM.render with an h1 reading Hello world! and the root element from getElementById.
Add a p element and observe the error, then wrap both in a div.
Open Babel's Try it out page and compare JSX with its compiled output.
task.expected_result: Page shows a heading and a paragraph generated entirely from JavaScript.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 36 - React.js/36.05 Introduction to JSX and Babel/my-react-app

pitfalls: Two sibling top-level elements in render cause a syntax error; wrap them.
Removing the React import (older setups) breaks JSX with React is not defined.
(Extra) Reference repo is a Vite app with React 18+/19, so index.js becomes main.jsx and ReactDOM.render is no longer used.

Tasks: 1) render an h1 into #root; 2) add a p and fix the multiple-root error with a wrapper; 3) rewrite the same output with React.createElement; 4) use a fragment instead of a div.
